predicate_definitions.artifact_valid: The evidence schema, source/build identity, hashes, ordering, dimensions, frames, and replay inputs validate.
predicate_definitions.solver_contract_valid: The intended VBD solver and backend ran every required step without fallback, invalid state, or an undisclosed cap.
predicate_definitions.physical_outcome_valid: A scenario-specific quantitative oracle passes for the declared duration and accuracy target.
predicate_definitions.manual_inspected: A current-build render or plot was actually inspected and records the expected qualitative behavior.
predicate_definitions.media_decoded: Required image/video media decodes for its declared duration and is bound to the validated run.
predicate_definitions.performance_comparable: Scene, precision, backend, hardware, compiler, timer boundary, warmup, aggregation, and achieved accuracy are matched.
predicate_definitions.claim_valid: Every predicate required by the row passes and the resulting claim stays within the demonstrated boundary.

blockers: The paper-shaped no-log tetrahedral kernel exists in isolation, but the public World VBD path forces the different shared FEM Stable Neo-Hookean energy. End-to-end paper-profile routing, a mutation-sensitive independent energy/trajectory oracle, paper scenes, CPU/CUDA correctness, and matched performance remain incomplete.
Focused damping coverage does not reproduce the paper coefficient sweep on both backends.
Narrow attachments exist, but the full constraint family and paper scenes are not closed on CPU and CUDA.

Static-obstacle and self-contact slices exist. Public rigid fixed-penalty VBD now clears every AVBD continuation inventory and pointer on entry, empty snapshots, solver-family transitions, and exceptional exits, while bounded collision capacities fail closed and survive replay. This lifecycle safety is not the paper's persistent force-element loop: VBD still queries only current penetrating contacts before the position solve and performs no periodic CCD/candidate refresh. Separated high-speed and refresh mutation tests, persistent force-element diagnostics, the paper collision corpus, and CUDA candidate parity remain incomplete.
Lagged friction is only partially integrated and lacks the full paper sweeps, self-contact coverage, and CUDA parity.
The formula has focused tests, but Figures 5-6 and the full CPU/CUDA trajectory comparison are not reproduced.

The serial accelerator exists, but the public multithreaded World path silently ignores both Chebyshev acceleration and its configured convergence tolerance. Multithreaded mutation tests, source-equivalent collision skip policy, CPU/CUDA trajectory parity, and Figure 7/17 achieved-accuracy performance closure are missing.
DART has deterministic coloring tests, but the paper mesh color counts and GPU scheduling evidence are incomplete.
The parallel foundation does not yet reproduce Figure 9 with matched recolored and non-recolored trajectories.
DART has no source-equivalent VBD tearing or fracture topology-change implementation and evidence packet.

CUDA mass-spring and tetrahedral slices now use a Sylvester positive-definite guard with adversarial indefinite and near-singular boundary tests. A reachable indefinite-element regression, public World routing without fallback, the full force/contact/friction kernel, and paper workloads remain incomplete.

The current strand is only TinyVBD-inspired: skip-spring stiffness is 1,000,000x too large, tip spacing and demo damping differ, and DART uses a different Hessian/solve policy. A source-matched CPU/CUDA scene, independent outcome oracle, and comparable timing packet are missing.

Public rigid VBD reuses the AVBD 6-DOF kernel in fixed-penalty mode, including its cached step-start Taylor contact C/J foundation and fail-closed continuation/capacity lifecycle. It still uses a pre-position discrete penetrating-contact query, no paper DCD/periodic-CCD refresh, and no persistent force-element loop. Source-equivalent rigid-block oracles, separated-contact mutation tests, rigid-chain/teapot reproductions, matched performance, and CUDA remain missing.
DART lacks one VBD solve coupling the paper's heterogeneous rigid, particle, and deformable representations.
The limitation is documented but has no controlled CPU/CUDA scaling reproduction against a global solver.
The historical high-ratio sweep exercises variational multibody integration, not VBD. The exact VBD 100-iteration versus converged limitation row is not reproduced on either backend.
